slides.title: Customer Satisfaction Performance Review
slides.speaker_note: 12-month KTV analysis covering all customer journeys with concrete improvement recommendations for management decision.

slides.title: Executive Summary

bullets: Maintenance journey achieves strong performance at 8.1 KTV—above our 8.0 excellence threshold
Breakdown & Repair journey scores 7.2, falling below the 7.5 attention threshold and representing our primary risk area
Purchase journey (7.8) and Customer Service (7.4) perform adequately but show clear opportunity for improvement
Root cause analysis reveals communication clarity and waiting time transparency as key satisfaction drivers
Strategic opportunity: replicate Maintenance excellence across underperforming journeys

slides.speaker_note: Key message: We have a proven model for high satisfaction in Maintenance. The challenge is scaling those practices to Breakdown and Customer Service.

slides.title: Customer Journey Performance Overview
slides.speaker_note: Note the 0.9-point gap between highest (Maintenance) and lowest (Breakdown). This is not marginal—it represents fundamentally different customer experiences.

slides.title: Success Blueprint: Maintenance Journey

bullets: Maintenance achieves 8.1 KTV through clear communication and predictable service delivery
Customers value scheduled appointments with confirmed time windows and proactive updates
Technicians consistently praised for punctuality and professional execution
Gas boiler maintenance contracts benefit from established routines and customer familiarity
Proven formula: clarity + predictability + professionalism = high satisfaction

slides.speaker_note: Maintenance is our benchmark. It proves we can deliver excellent customer experiences when process and communication are aligned.

slides.title: Critical Challenge: Breakdown Journey

bullets: Breakdown & Repair scores 7.2, driven by inherent customer stress during service disruption
Waiting times for technician arrival and parts delivery create frustration and uncertainty
Unclear next steps and status updates amplify customer anxiety during breakdown situations
Heat pump and boiler breakdowns particularly challenging due to heating dependency
Gap to Maintenance (0.9 points) indicates fixable process issues, not technical capability

slides.speaker_note: Customers don't expect instant repairs—they expect transparency. The problem isn't our technical response; it's communication during uncertainty.

slides.title: Root Cause Analysis

bullets: Clear communication and punctuality are the strongest drivers of satisfaction across all journeys
Waiting times damage satisfaction only when combined with unclear status updates or uncertain timelines
Purchase journey (7.8) succeeds because onboarding sets clear expectations from the start
Customer Service (7.4) faces similar challenges to Breakdown: responsiveness perceived as slow despite friendly interactions
Pattern: customers reward transparency and predictability, penalize uncertainty

slides.speaker_note: This is the insight: satisfaction correlates more strongly with communication quality than with technical outcomes. Fix communication, fix satisfaction.

slides.title: Strategic Assessment

left_column.heading: What Works
items: Maintenance journey delivers 8.1+ satisfaction through structured communication
Purchase onboarding creates clear customer expectations
Technical quality and end results consistently meet customer needs

right_column.heading: What Needs Attention
items: Breakdown journey requires proactive status updates and clearer timelines
Customer Service response times need improvement or better expectation setting
Waiting time transparency missing across multiple touchpoints

slides.speaker_note: Left side shows we know how to deliver. Right side shows where to apply that knowledge. This is an execution gap, not a capability gap.

slides.title: Action Plan: Close the Experience Gap

content.recommendation: Deploy Maintenance journey communication standards to Breakdown and Customer Service, focusing on proactive updates and clear timeline expectations
rationale: Maintenance journey proves that structured communication drives satisfaction—we have the blueprint
Breakdown and Customer Service share the same root issue: customers lack visibility into progress and next steps
Communication improvements require minimal investment compared to operational changes, yet deliver measurable satisfaction gains
next_steps: Implement automated status updates for breakdown service requests (ETA, technician assigned, parts ordered)
Adopt Maintenance-style confirmation protocols for customer service interactions (expected resolution time, follow-up schedule)
Establish KTV monitoring dashboard with journey-specific targets and monthly review cadence
Conduct customer feedback sessions specifically on heat pump and solar panel service experiences to identify product-specific pain points

slides.speaker_note: This is a scale problem, not an innovation problem. We're not asking for new capabilities—we're replicating what already works in Maintenance.

slides.title: Methodology & Context

items: KTV measured on 1-10 scale, collected post-interaction across all customer touchpoints
Performance benchmarks: >8.0 considered strong, <7.5 requires attention
Journeys analyzed: Maintenance, Breakdown & Repair, Purchase, Customer Service
Products in scope: Gas boiler maintenance contracts, Heat pumps, Solar panels

slides.speaker_note: All scores validated through customer feedback system. Qualitative insights based on verbatim analysis and support ticket themes.
